Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Q2 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Q2 FY2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; and Taylor Kim, Chief Revenue Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge's performance for Q2 FY2024. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our ForgeAI platform and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on four key areas: accelerating new customer acquisition, sustaining robust MRR growth, enhancing our LTV to CAC ratio, and maintaining disciplined operating expenses.

On new customer acquisition, we saw tremendous momentum, adding hundreds of net new logos that directly boosted our ARR and MRR. MRR trends were equally impressive, with acceleration in both new logo and expansion contributions amid resilient demand. Our LTV/CAC ratio strengthened notably, reflecting better unit economics across segments. And on expenses, we leveraged our scale effectively while investing in high-impact areas.

We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan to discuss the financials in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $285 million, representing a 28% increase year-over-year and 9% quarter-over-quarter, driven by 32% ARR growth to $1.15 billion and a robust 118% Net Revenue Retention rate. Our Rule of 40 score stands at 62, reflecting strong growth offset by disciplined expense management. Our gross margin expanded to 82%, and non-GAAP operating income reached $47 million.

Let me start with our operating expense breakdown on a non-GAAP basis. Total OpEx was $238 million in the quarter, or 83% of revenue, down 200 basis points year-over-year from 85%. This improvement underscores our focus on operational leverage as we scale toward $2 billion in ARR over the next few years. Excluding stock-based compensation and related employer payroll taxes, which totaled $42 million—or about 18% of non-GAAP OpEx—our cash OpEx came in at $196 million.

Breaking it down by line item, with key trends, drivers, and initiatives: Research and Development came in at $72 million, or 25% of revenue, up 18% year-over-year and 5% quarter-over-quarter. R&D remains our largest investment area, reflecting our commitment to product leadership in a competitive landscape similar to Salesforce's Einstein AI or ServiceNow's Vancouver platform releases. Year-over-year, this moderates from the 35% growth in FY2023, as we lap heavier post-IPO hiring from 2022. Headcount grew modestly by 4% quarter-over-quarter to 1,850 engineers and product roles, with efficiency gains from a shift to a senior-heavy team—average tenure now at 4.2 years. We're directing about 45% of R&D spend to core platform enhancements, including the next-gen ForgeAI engine for generative AI-driven no-code workflow orchestration. This is live in beta with 15 early enterprise customers, like a Fortune 50 bank, delivering 3x faster deployment times versus legacy tools. Regionally, 60% of R&D is U.S.-based in our Seattle and Austin hubs, but we're increasing EMEA engineering in Dublin by 20% for GDPR-compliant AI features, supporting a 25% year-over-year rise in EU ARR. APAC investments are at 10% of spend, emphasizing localization for surging low-code demand in Japan and India. Long-term, we're aiming for 22-24% of revenue, below the industry median of 28% for peers like Snowflake or Datadog, positioning us for 130%+ NRR via innovations like agentic AI agents automating 40% of routine enterprise tasks—early pilots generating $5 million in upsell pipeline.

Sales & Marketing was $112 million, or 39% of revenue, up 22% year-over-year but flat quarter-over-quarter. This remains our growth engine, with dollar-based S&M efficiency improving to 1.15x from 0.95x year-over-year, and CAC payback compressing to 16 months from 20 months—mirroring HubSpot and ZoomInfo's enterprise motion shifts. Sales rep productivity reached $1.8 million ARR per quota carrier, up 12% year-over-year, thanks to a revamped inside sales model combining AI lead scoring with human engagement—conversion from MQL to SQL up 15%. Marketing, at 12% of revenue, grew pipeline 45% year-over-year via events like Dreamforce partnerships and ABM in financial services. U.S. is 70% of S&M at $78 million, EMEA 20% at $22 million up 35% year-over-year on wins like a €50 million deal with a major German auto OEM, and APAC 10% at $11 million ramping with Singapore hires targeting 50% regional ARR growth. We added 120 net quota carriers, but expect S&M to moderate to 36-38% of revenue in H2 as we expand from our 1,200+ customer base averaging $900k ACV. Excluding SBC at 22% of S&M, cash efficiency shines brighter.

General & Administrative was $54 million, or 19% of revenue, up 12% year-over-year and 3% quarter-over-quarter. This is our most leveraged line, scaling at less than half our revenue growth rate, now matching mature SaaS leaders like Workday at 19% versus 22% last year. Headcount stayed flat at 650 roles, with 15% attrition offset by automation. Professional fees rose 8% for audit, compliance, SEC filings, and SOX controls; IT and facilities increased modestly with hybrid work. SBC is lighter at 12%. U.S.-centric at 75%, EMEA G&A up 18% for local tax and HR as international revenue hits 25%; APAC under 5% for GTM support. Long-term target is 16-18% using our internal Forge platform for procure-to-pay, cutting approval cycles 50% and freeing cash for R&D and repurchases—we bought back $50 million in shares this quarter at $45 average.

Overall, OpEx shows R&D innovation, scalable S&M growth, and G&A leverage—non-GAAP OpEx down 200 basis points year-over-year, free cash flow margins at 28%, setting us up for profitability amid macro like high rates on SMBs, with enterprise resilience.

Next, our key efficiency metrics, including Lifetime Value to Customer Acquisition Cost ratio, or LTV/CAC, which hit 4.2x this quarter, up from 3.8x last quarter and our best since Q1 last year. This measures expected customer lifetime value—factoring ARR, net retention, gross margins—against fully loaded acquisition costs including sales, marketing, and onboarding. Above 3x signals health in SaaS; we're expanding. Average LTV per customer was $48,000: Q3 ARR per customer $12,000 times 82% gross margin (from AWS multi-tenant efficiencies) divided by 4.2% annualized churn, implying 60-month LTV for enterprise cohorts. CAC was $11,400 per new customer, down 8% quarter-over-quarter via 15% cuts in paid channels like Google Ads and LinkedIn, boosted by organic.

This stems from three levers on our AI collaboration platform serving 5,000+ global teams, rivaling Slack Enterprise Grid and Asana premium. First, PLG acceleration: doubled freemium-to-paid via AI feature gating (unlocks at 50 active bots), lifting self-serve 22%, SMB CAC to under $2,500, viral coefficient 1.3x via Teams and Workspace integrations—no outbound for <$50k ARR. Second, retention/expansion: NRR to 118% from 115% via churn prediction with LLM sentiment on in-app data; enterprise (65% of $220M ARR) expanded 28% on Advanced Security (SOC 2, GDPR); 12-month cohort at 92% retention vs. 85% industry. North America 4.5x LTV/CAC with $2M ARR Fortune 100 win like Salesforce land-and-expand; EMEA 4.0x with UK/Germany GTM and DACH pricing (€15/user); APAC 3.2x but improving via LINE/Atlassian partnerships targeting 20% CAC cut. Q4 guide 4.5x on AI upsell (30% beta attach) and Q1 generative AI release countering Copilot. Ahead of Monday.com's 3.5x.

We continue investing in R&D to drive innovation and expand offerings. Cash position remains strong at $450 million, providing flexibility for acquisitions and growth.

Turning to MRR trends, the core of our SaaS predictability. Ending MRR reached $95.8 million for Q2 FY2024, up 28% year-over-year from $74.7 million, accelerating from 24% in Q1, and 8% sequential from Q1 ahead of 4-5% guide, compounding land-and-expand.

Components via dollar-based metrics: New Logo MRR $17.2 million, up 35% year-over-year, from Enterprise AI Analytics Suite launch resonating like Adobe Sensei or Einstein; wins like $1.2M financial services migrating from Tableau, mid-market healthcare $150k ACV. Expansion MRR $9.1 million, 53% year-over-year best ever, NRR 118% up 300bps above 110% benchmark; upsells to AI workflow with multi-year from logistics client 2.5x on Oracle ERP. Churn/Contraction net $4.2 million or 0.8% annualized, stable, down from 1.1% YoY despite SMB pressures like Zendesk; 85% MRR enterprise sticky, contraction <4%. North America 62% ($59.4M) 26% YoY fintech/retail; EMEA 24% ($23M) 32% YoY GDPR/Paris DC (40% latency cut); APAC 14% ($13.4M) 45% YoY LINE/MYOB. 'AI Everywhere' with AWS Bedrock/Vertex AI boosts LTV/CAC to 4.2x; multi-product 42% customers (up from 35%) NDR >120%. Q3 30%+ YoY on 50% AI pipeline, despite USD forex.

On new customer acquisition, we added 452 net new customers, up 28% year-over-year from 353, exceeding 400-425 guide, affirming product-market fit for AI workflow in hybrid/digital shifts. Net new ARR $12.4 million, 32% YoY from $9.4 million; MRR $1.03 million. ACV $27,500 up 12% YoY, enterprise (>100k) 62% vs 55%, SMB/mid 38% for land-and-expand. North America 68% (308 logos) financials/Salesforce/Workday integrations; EMEA 45% YoY (92) telcos/5G; APAC 52% YoY (52) AWS Marketplace Japan/Australia; LatAm early Brazil. ForgeAI Agent Q1 launch 40% inbound lift, 22% freemium conversion like GitHub Copilot; 15 ISV integrations (Snowflake/Zoom) 25% new ARR; rev ops CAC payback 11 months from 14. Cohort NRR 118% first 90 days, usage AI pricing. Q3 475-525 adds, $13.5-14.5M new ARR on IT budgets like Atlassian/monday.com; multi-year 65%, healthcare adjacents mitigate SMB churn. Fueled 45% total ARR growth to record $1.15 billion, 31% YoY; top-quartile per Bessemer.

We are updating our full-year guidance to reflect our strong first half. We now expect revenue to be in the range of $1.12 billion to $1.16 billion, with ARR growth of 30% and NRR above 115%.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to ask a question at this time, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. Our first question comes from Mike Ross with Goldman Sachs.

Mike Ross:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of ForgeAI on your overall growth?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, Mike. ForgeAI has been transformative, acting as our generative AI copilot for no-code workflows, directly fueling 40% of inbound leads and contributing over 30% to new ARR this quarter through betas and pilots. It's driven expansions in existing accounts, with 28% NRR uplift in early adopters, and positioned us competitively against Copilot or Einstein by slashing deployment times 3x. We've seen it accelerate PLG conversions by 22% and boost viral growth, making up a key part of our 28% revenue beat. Excited for broader rollout in Q4.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen:
What are your plans for international expansion?

Taylor Kim:
Great question, Lisa. International is a major growth driver, now 38% of revenue. We're ramping EMEA with 20% engineering in Dublin for GDPR AI, targeting 32% YoY MRR growth via Paris DC and DACH pricing—recent €50M auto OEM win exemplifies. APAC fastest at 45-52% YoY customer adds, hiring Singapore managers, partnerships like LINE Japan and Atlassian Australia for 20% MRR share by FY2026. LatAm localization Brazil early. Overall, 50% regional ARR growth via AWS Marketplace co-sell, localized GTM, aiming for 45% of total revenue in two years while leveraging 118% global NRR.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Patel with JPMorgan.

David Patel:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, David. Churn remains low at 0.8% annualized dollar-based, stable sequential and down YoY, far below benchmarks. Enterprise focus (85% MRR) with sticky use cases like mission-critical AI workflows keeps contraction under 4%. Proactive LLM churn prediction on in-app sentiment drives 118% NRR, 92% 12-month retention vs. 85% industry. Multi-year contracts now 65% new ACV, upsells like Advanced Security. SMB pressures from rates mitigated by PLG efficiencies and cohort focus—monitoring but resilient like peers.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
